close_reason: Landed. Added WsSender (owns sink, has send_text/send_request) and WsReceiver (owns stream, has next_frame), plus WsSession::split(self) -> (WsSender, WsReceiver). WsSession's unified methods preserve backward compat by delegating to embedded halves — additive shape, no public-API break. Compile-time Send check + integration test (tests/ws_split_smoke.rs against a real tokio_tungstenite server on 127.0.0.1:0) exercise the concurrent-send-while-receiving topology that the unified &mut self handle could not service.
description:
ws/mod.rs:101-104 — WsSession { sink, stream }

WsSession is constructed by splitting a tokio_tungstenite::WebSocketStream into sink and stream halves. Internally it has both halves in one struct, with all methods taking `&mut self`:

  - next_frame(&mut self) -> ... 
  - send_text(&mut self, text: String) -> ...
  - send_request(&mut self, req, id) -> ...

Concurrency contract gaps:

1. **Cannot send while receiving.** A caller needs `&mut WsSession` to call next_frame() and ALSO to call send_request(). These borrows are exclusive — a typical pattern (one task receiving in a loop, another task occasionally sending) cannot work because both require &mut. The caller must either:
   - serialize all access through a single task that interleaves send and receive
   - or store the WsSession behind an Arc<Mutex<_>> and lock-then-await — which holds the mutex across .await, blocking the receive task while the send task waits for the network

2. **The split exists internally but is not exposed.** The implementation already has them as separate halves; a future split(self) -> (WsSender, WsReceiver) method that returns owned halves would unlock the common one-receive-task + one-send-task topology. The doc-comment says "Call next_frame in a loop to receive events. Use send_request to transmit JMAP requests." but doesn't address the concurrent-send case — a caller reading the docs would assume single-threaded use is the only supported model.

This is exactly the kind of "would the next on-call rotation curse your name" finding: a caller designing a chat client around this API will hit the concurrency wall on first sprint and have to rewrite around Mutex<WsSession> or some other crutch. Every real-world WebSocket consumer needs concurrent send-while-receiving.

Recommendation: in the next minor release, add WsSession::split(self) -> (WsSender, WsReceiver). The existing WsSession can stay as the convenience handle. The new types are #[non_exhaustive] from day one. This avoids breaking the v0.x callers who use the unified handle while unblocking concurrent-send for everyone else.
title: WsSession provides no concurrent-send safety — sink and stream are split but both behind &mut self
